title: Module 8 intro — Run, Monitor, and Maintain

lines: Welcome to Module Eight: Run, Monitor, and Maintain.
Shipping an agent is where the real job starts.
Picture QuickBite, a food delivery app with an AI support agent for late orders and refunds.
At launch it works well, and the team moves on.

say.0: Picture Quick Bite, a food delivery app with an AI support agent for late orders and refunds.

lines: For a month, nobody deploys anything, and the logs show no errors.
Every dashboard stays green.
Yet refunds creep up, and steps per chat climb from four to eight.
The cost of each resolved ticket doubles.
Nobody notices until customers complain.
Their monitoring could say a chat took nine seconds, but never why.
So they add agent traces, where every model call and tool call becomes a span.
Each span records the prompt version, tokens, cost, and the tool's exact arguments.
Within minutes, the pattern appears.
A partner's order-status tool had changed its format, so the agent retried, gave up, and refunded.
They switch to a safe fallback, fix the tool, and add the case to their golden test set.
A scheduled contract test now checks that tool every day.
Lesson one is observability: what every span must carry.
OpenTelemetry lets you instrument once and send the same traces to any backend.

say.1: Open Telemetry lets you instrument once and send the same traces to any back end.

lines: You'll learn which signals to alert on, like task success, tool errors, and steps per task.
The one that matters most is cost per resolved task.
You'll also capture feedback, from thumbs to quiet signs like rephrasing.
Tied to traces, it feeds a data flywheel.
Lesson two covers four kinds of drift: input, corpus, model, and tool.
Agents degrade even when nobody touches them.
The fixes: pin model versions, run a golden set against production on a schedule, and contract-test every tool.
Track each metric against a baseline.
When an incident hits: contain, diagnose from traces, fix the right layer, and add a regression test.
Then ask what guard would have caught it sooner.
Prompts, schemas, and model versions are versioned together, then ship through shadow, canary, and full rollout.
Even a one-word prompt edit is a production change.
This domain is five percent of the exam, and a classic question is an agent that degrades with no deployment: the answer is an upstream change.
Let's start with lesson one, observability for agents.
